paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: This plot, titled 'Errors (RTE)', illustrates the generalization errors on the RTE dataset as a function of adapter rank. The x-axis is labeled 'Rank' and uses a logarithmic scale with tick marks at 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis displays error values on a linear scale with tick marks at 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9, ranging approximately from 0.3 to just above 0.6. A single black solid line with green circular markers connects the four data points, and each data point includes vertical error bars. The line begins at a rank of 4 with an error of approximately 0.34, dips slightly to its lowest value of approximately 0.31 at rank 16, then increases to approximately 0.40 at rank 64, and rises more steeply to approximately 0.61 at rank 256. The error bars are relatively small at all points, with the largest appearing at rank 256.
